No source-supported demonstration for dimensions 11-15 is given.

issues.title: Claim of computational advantage up to 15 assets is not supported by the stated experiments

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed RQMC error formula subtracts Q^{RQMC}_{N,d}[g], which is not defined in the source. The defined randomized estimator is Q^{RQMC}_{N,S,d}[g]. As written, the standard error is not well-defined for the estimator being analyzed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Q^{RQMC}_{N,d}[g] by the defined overall RQMC estimator Q^{RQMC}_{N,S,d}[g].
issues.overall_effect: The practical RQMC error estimate and confidence interval are unreliable because the formula refers to an undefined object.
issues.title: RQMC error estimate uses an undefined estimator
issues.why_classification: A local notational repair restores the intended error estimate without changing the method or guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By symmetry of the integrand $g(\cdot)$ and the proposal density $\psi^{nor}(\cdot)$ around the origin, it is sufficient to control the behavior of the transformed integrand as $u_j \to 0$ to ensure that it is also controlled at all $2^d$ corners of $[0,1]^d$.

issues.failure_explanation: The integrand g(y;R) is not generally even for the non-even payoffs considered (basket put, call on min) and for nonzero damping vectors R. Therefore the one-sided boundary analysis at u_j -> 0 does not follow from the stated symmetry argument.

failure_location.quote: the original integrand in \eqref{g_integrand} is even (a consequence of Fourier transform properties).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the evenness argument with a direct two-sided boundary analysis (u_j -> 0 and u_j -> 1), or impose hypotheses that make the integrand genuinely symmetric.
issues.overall_effect: The justification that controlling the u_j -> 0 boundary controls all corners is unsupported for the general payoffs and damping parameters used.
issues.title: False symmetry claim used to reduce boundary analysis to one side
issues.why_classification: The intended boundary conditions can likely be repaired by a local additional argument, but the source's stated inference is mathematically invalid.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed GBM increment characteristic function used in the ratio has an extra real factor exp(rT) and the wrong linear term. In particular it equals exp(rT) at z=0, whereas a characteristic function must equal 1 at z=0. This conflicts with the GBM characteristic function stated in the model table.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the univariate GBM characteristic function to exp(i z (r - sigma^2/2)T - T sigma^2 z^2/2) and redo the ratio expansion.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit expression for r^{GBM}_j(u_j) and the algebraic derivation of the GBM independent boundary condition are based on a false formula.
issues.title: Incorrect univariate GBM characteristic function in the ratio derivation
issues.why_classification: The final boundary condition is recoverable by a local correction to the characteristic function and algebra, without changing the proposed method.

issues.failure_explanation: Expanding the multivariate GBM characteristic function at z = x + iR and dividing by the Gaussian proposal density produces an additional imaginary term -i T x' Sigma R in the bounded factor. The displayed h_2^{GBM}(u) omits this term, so the stated equality for r^{GBM}(u) is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing imaginary linear term (or correct the algebraic expansion) in the definition of h_2^{GBM}.
issues.overall_effect: The dependent GBM boundary-growth derivation uses an incorrect intermediate expression, although the boundedness conclusion is not affected.
issues.title: Missing term in the dependent GBM ratio expansion
issues.why_classification: This is a local algebraic correction; the advertised boundary condition and method remain intact.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposed formula for tilde sigma_j contains the exponent T/(nu - 2T), which is undefined when nu = 2T. This is a legitimate parameter value in the stated model regime, and no limiting or special-case choice is provided.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Handle nu = 2T separately by evaluating the appropriate limit or reparameterizing, or explicitly exclude that boundary case.
issues.overall_effect: The VG domain-transformation parameter rule is incomplete at the boundary nu = 2T.
issues.title: VG parameter rule undefined at nu = 2T
issues.why_classification: This is a degenerate-case omission that can be fixed locally without changing the main construction.

issues.failure_explanation: The derived univariate VG condition says the boundary is finite only when tilde nu is at most the critical value 2T/nu - 1, and diverges when tilde nu is larger. The summary rule chooses tilde nu = critical value + epsilon with epsilon >= 0, which violates the condition for any positive epsilon. The floor remark for negative critical values has the same problem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the rule to choose tilde nu at or below the critical value (e.g., critical value - epsilon with a valid lower bound) and restrict or reprove the short-maturity regime where the critical value is nonpositive.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised VG tuning rule does not guarantee the claimed bounded transformed integrand in the stated parameter range.
issues.title: VG independent parameter direction contradicts the derived boundary condition
issues.why_classification: The correction is a contained parameter-regime fix, but it changes the advertised tuning rule and may require excluding short maturities, so it is more than a trivial typo repair.

issues.failure_explanation: The large-y expansion of the VG characteristic function factor has the wrong constant and linear terms. From the stated VG CF, factoring out (nu/2)x'Sigma x gives a constant term 1 + nu R'theta - (nu/2)R'Sigma R and an imaginary linear term involving (nu R'Sigma - nu theta')x; the displayed numerator instead contains -nu theta'(i x - R) and omits the required +nu R'theta structure. Thus the asymptotic relation is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rederive the asymptotic expansion of the VG characteristic function with the correct signs and factors, then re-verify the boundary conditions.
issues.overall_effect: The dependent VG boundary-growth conditions are not established by the displayed asymptotic step.
issues.title: Algebraically invalid asymptotic expansion of the dependent VG characteristic function
issues.why_classification: The final matrix conditions may be recoverable, but the source's derivation is invalid and requires a nontrivial correction of the asymptotic argument.

issues.failure_explanation: As printed, the nested integral contains an unexplained factor 1/w in the inner integrand. Separately, the proof's normal-mixture step uses Z ~ N(0, tilde Sigma) with the standard chi density, whereas the proposition's L is defined from tilde nu * tilde Sigma. For the stated Student-t density, the standard-chi mixture requires covariance tilde nu * tilde Sigma (or a scaled chi density), so the proof does not establish the stated identity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the spurious 1/w factor (if unintended) and correct the mixture representation by using N(0, tilde nu * tilde Sigma) with the standard chi density, or the correctly scaled chi density with N(0, tilde Sigma).
issues.overall_effect: The VG dependent domain-transformation representation is unreliable as written, affecting the hybrid VG quadrature built on it.
issues.title: VG proposition statement/proof mixture representation is inconsistent
issues.why_classification: The proposition can be repaired by a contained correction to the mixture scaling and the displayed formula, but the labelled result is not valid as written.

issues.failure_explanation: Using the source's definition hat P(z) = integral e^{i z'x} P(x) dx, the one-dimensional transform of the basket put (1 - e^x)^+ is 1/(i z (1 + i z)) in the half-plane where the integral converges, not Gamma(-i z)/Gamma(-i z + 2) = 1/(1 - i z). The stated domains are also sign-reversed relative to the damping implied by this definition. Thus the table's payoff transforms do not follow from the stated payoffs and Fourier transform convention.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the payoff transforms and delta_P with expressions consistent with the stated Fourier convention and payoffs, or change the convention consistently throughout the paper.
issues.overall_effect: The Fourier-space integrands used for the stated payoffs are false, undermining the numerical pricing results that rely on them.
issues.title: Payoff Fourier transforms and analyticity domains are inconsistent with the stated transform
issues.why_classification: The incorrect transforms affect the core pricing integrals for all payoffs, and the source does not provide the corrected multivariate formulas or a consistent convention repair.

issues.failure_explanation: The example claims that the componentwise mu_{NIG,i} makes the discounted assets martingales. For the multivariate dynamics with common inverse Gaussian subordinator and covariance structure involving Delta, the required exponential moment and drift correction depend on the full vector beta and the matrix Delta, not on beta_i alone. As written, the martingale condition is not established and is false in general for d > 1 or non-identity Delta.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide the correct multivariate martingale drift depending on beta and Delta, or restrict the NIG example to d = 1 with Delta = 1.
issues.overall_effect: The NIG model definition is internally inconsistent with its stated characteristic function and martingale assumption.
issues.title: NIG martingale correction is not multivariate consistent
issues.why_classification: The defect can be contained to the model definition and drift formula, but as written the stated NIG multi-asset model is not valid.
